Adhyāya 19

Sanskrit

एकोनविंशो ऽध्यायः

ekonaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ

English

Chapter Nineteen1

Sanskrit

पुत्र उवाच

putra uvāca

English

19.1–5The son said: Having heard the sage's words2, Kārtavīrya3, lord of men, went to Dattātreya's hermitage and worshipped him with devotion: by massaging his feet and the like, by bringing honey and the like, by bringing garlands, sandalwood and the like, perfumes, water, fruits and the like, by preparing food, and by removing his leftovers. The sage, pleased, spoke to him, the devotee, in just the way the gods were told long ago4: "Enjoyment of liquor and the like is blameworthy, and because this woman is seated at my side, enjoyment of her too is blameworthy. I am always [so]. You should not obstruct me, who am unable, in this way. For help, worship one who is able, sir."5

19.1

Sanskrit

इत्यृषेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा कार्तवीर्यो नरेश्वरः । दत्तात्रेयाश्रमं गत्त्वा तं भक्त्या समपूजयत् ॥

ityṛṣervacanaṃ śrutvā kārtavīryo nareśvaraḥ | dattātreyāśramaṃ gattvā taṃ bhaktyā samapūjayat ||

English

Its English is given with 19.1–5, above.

19.2

Sanskrit

पादसंवाहनाद्येन मध्वाद्याहरणेन च । स्त्रक्चन्दनादिगन्धाम्बुफलाद्यनयनेन च ॥

pādasaṃvāhanādyena madhvādyāharaṇena ca | strakcandanādigandhāmbuphalādyanayanena ca ||

English

Its English is given with 19.1–5, above.

19.3

Sanskrit

तथान्नसाधनैस्तस्य उच्छिष्टापोहनेन च । परितुष्टो मुनिर्भूतं तमुवाच तथैव सः ॥

tathānnasādhanaistasya ucchiṣṭāpohanena ca | parituṣṭo munirbhūtaṃ tamuvāca tathaiva saḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 19.1–5, above.

19.4

Sanskrit

यथैवोक्ताः पुरा देवा मद्यभोगादिकुत्सनम् । स्त्री चेयं मम पार्श्वस्थेत्येतद्भोगाच्च कुत्सितम् ॥

yathaivoktāḥ purā devā madyabhogādikutsanam | strī ceyaṃ mama pārśvasthetyetadbhogācca kutsitam ||

English

Its English is given with 19.1–5, above.

19.5

Sanskrit

सदैवाहं न मामेवमुपरोद्धुं त्वमर्हसि । अशक्तमुपकाराय शक्तमाराधयस्व भोः ॥

sadaivāhaṃ na māmevamuparoddhuṃ tvamarhasi | aśaktamupakārāya śaktamārādhayasva bhoḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 19.1–5, above.

19.6

Sanskrit

जड उवाच तेनैवमुक्तो मुनिना स्मृत्वा गर्गवचश्च तत् । प्रत्युवाच प्रणम्यैनं सार्तवीर्यार्जुनस्तदा ॥

jaḍa uvāca tenaivamukto muninā smṛtvā gargavacaśca tat | pratyuvāca praṇamyainaṃ sārtavīryārjunastadā ||

English

Jaḍa said: Thus addressed by the sage, and remembering that saying of Garga6 as well, Sārtavīrya Arjuna7 then bowed to him and replied.8

Sanskrit

अर्जुन उवाच

arjuna uvāca

English

19.7Arjuna said: "Why do you bewilder me, O god, having resorted to your own māyā9? You are sinless, and so is this goddess, the source of all existence10.11

19.7

Sanskrit

किं मां मोहयसे देव ! स्वां मायां समुपाश्रितः । अनघस्त्वं तथैवेयं देवी सर्वभवारणिः ॥

kiṃ māṃ mohayase deva ! svāṃ māyāṃ samupāśritaḥ | anaghastvaṃ tathaiveyaṃ devī sarvabhavāraṇiḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 19.7, above.

19.8

Sanskrit

इत्युक्तः प्रीतिमान् देवस्ततस्तं प्रत्युवाच ह । कार्तवीर्यं महाभागं वशीकृतमहीतलम् ॥

ityuktaḥ prītimān devastatastaṃ pratyuvāca ha | kārtavīryaṃ mahābhāgaṃ vaśīkṛtamahītalam ||

English

Thus addressed, the god12, pleased, then replied to him, to Kārtavīrya, the greatly fortunate13 one, who had subjugated the surface of the earth.14

19.9

Sanskrit

वरं वृणीष्व गुह्यं मे यत् त्वया समुदीरितम् । तेन तुष्टिः परा जाता त्वय्यद्य मम पार्थिव ॥

varaṃ vṛṇīṣva guhyaṃ me yat tvayā samudīritam | tena tuṣṭiḥ parā jātā tvayyadya mama pārthiva ||

English

"Choose a boon. My secret, which has been declared aloud by you15: by that a supreme satisfaction with you has arisen in me today, O king."16

19.10

Sanskrit

ये च मां पूजयिष्यन्ति गन्धमाल्यादिभिर्नराः । मांसमद्योपहारैश्च मिष्टान्नैश्चाज्यसंयुतैः ॥

ye ca māṃ pūjayiṣyanti gandhamālyādibhirnarāḥ | māṃsamadyopahāraiśca miṣṭānnaiścājyasaṃyutaiḥ ||

English

And those men who will worship me with fragrant substances, garlands and the like, with offerings of meat and liquor, and with sweet foods mixed with ghee17,18

19.11

Sanskrit

लक्ष्मीसमेतं गीतैश्च ब्राह्मणानां तथार्च्चनैः । वाद्यैर्मनोरमैर्वोणावेणुशङ्कादिभिस्तथा ॥

lakṣmīsametaṃ gītaiśca brāhmaṇānāṃ tathārccanaiḥ | vādyairmanoramairvoṇāveṇuśaṅkādibhistathā ||

English

[those men who will worship] me, accompanied by Lakṣmī19, with songs and likewise with the honouring of brāhmaṇas20, and with charming music of the lute21, flute, conch and the like22†

19.12

Sanskrit

तेषामहं परां तुष्टिं पुत्रदारधनादिकम् । प्रदास्याम्यवघातञ्च हनिष्याम्यवमन्यताम् ॥

teṣāmahaṃ parāṃ tuṣṭiṃ putradāradhanādikam | pradāsyāmyavaghātañca haniṣyāmyavamanyatām ||

English

To them I shall give supreme satisfaction, [together with] sons, wife, wealth and the like, and I shall destroy the assault of those who scorn [them]23.24†

19.13

Sanskrit

स त्वं वरय भद्रं ते वरं यन्मसेप्सितम् । प्रसादसुमुखस्ते ऽहं गुह्यनामप्रकीर्तनात् ॥

sa tvaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varaṃ yanmasepsitam | prasādasumukhaste 'haṃ guhyanāmaprakīrtanāt ||

English

So you, choose a boon25, the one that you desire in [your] mind26; may good fortune be yours. I am graciously well disposed toward you because of the proclaiming of my secret name27.28

Sanskrit

कार्तवीर्य उवाच

kārtavīrya uvāca

English

19.14Kārtavīrya said: "If you are gracious to me, O god, then grant me that supreme prosperity by which I may protect my subjects and yet incur no adharma29."30

19.14

Sanskrit

यदि देव प्रसन्नस्त्वं तत् प्रयच्छर्धिमुत्तमाम् । यया प्रजाः पालये ऽहं न चाधर्ममवाप्नुयाम् ॥

yadi deva prasannastvaṃ tat prayacchardhimuttamām | yayā prajāḥ pālaye 'haṃ na cādharmamavāpnuyām ||

English

Its English is given with 19.14, above.

19.15

Sanskrit

परानुसरणे ज्ञानमप्रतिद्वन्द्वतां रणे । सहस्रमाप्तुमिच्छामि बाहूनां लघुतागुणम् ॥

parānusaraṇe jñānamapratidvandvatāṃ raṇe | sahasramāptumicchāmi bāhūnāṃ laghutāguṇam ||

English

I wish to obtain knowledge in tracking down others31, freedom from any rival in battle, a thousand arms, and the quality of lightness32 [in wielding] those arms.33

19.16

Sanskrit

असङ्गा गतयः सन्तु शैलाकाशाम्बुभूमिषु । पातालेषु च सर्वेषु वधश्चाप्यधिकान्नरात् ॥

asaṅgā gatayaḥ santu śailākāśāmbubhūmiṣu | pātāleṣu ca sarveṣu vadhaścāpyadhikānnarāt ||

English

May my movements be unobstructed on mountains, in the sky, in water and on earth, and in all the nether worlds34; and may my death come from a man who is superior [to me]35.36

19.17

Sanskrit

तथोन्मार्गप्रवृत्तस्य चास्तु सन्मार्गदेशकः । सन्तु मे ऽतिथयः श्लाघ्या वित्तदाने तथाक्षये ॥

tathonmārgapravṛttasya cāstu sanmārgadeśakaḥ | santu me 'tithayaḥ ślāghyā vittadāne tathākṣaye ||

English

Likewise, for one who has set out on a wrong path37, may there be a guide to the good path. May I have guests who are praiseworthy in the giving of wealth and likewise in [its] inexhaustibility38.39

19.18

Sanskrit

अनष्टद्रव्यता राष्ट्रे ममानुस्मरणेन च । त्वयि भक्तिर्ममैवास्तु नित्यमव्यभिचारिणी ॥

anaṣṭadravyatā rāṣṭre mamānusmaraṇena ca | tvayi bhaktirmamaivāstu nityamavyabhicāriṇī ||

English

May there be no loss of property in the realm, and [this] through remembrance of me40; and may my own devotion41 to you be constant and unfailing.42

Sanskrit

दत्तात्रेय उवाच

dattātreya uvāca

English

19.19Dattātreya said: "You will obtain all those boons that you have declared here, and by my grace you will become a cakravartin43, a sovereign lord."44

19.19

Sanskrit

यत्र ते कीर्तिताः सर्वे तान् वरान् समवाप्स्यसि । मत्प्रसादाच्च भविता चक्रवर्तो त्वमीश्वरः ॥

yatra te kīrtitāḥ sarve tān varān samavāpsyasi | matprasādācca bhavitā cakravarto tvamīśvaraḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 19.19, above.

Sanskrit

जड उवाच

jaḍa uvāca

19.20

Sanskrit

प्रणिपत्य ततस्तस्मै दत्तात्रेयाय सो ऽर्जुनः । आनाय्य प्रकृतीः सम्यगभिषेकमगृह्णत ॥

praṇipatya tatastasmai dattātreyāya so 'rjunaḥ | ānāyya prakṛtīḥ samyagabhiṣekamagṛhṇata ||

English

19.20–21Then that Arjuna bowed down to Dattātreya and, having properly summoned the prakṛtis45, received the consecration46. Established in the kingdom, that Haihaya47, who had obtained supreme prosperity from Dattātreya and was endowed with exceeding might, then made a proclamation:48

19.21

Sanskrit

आघोषयामास तदा स्थितो राज्ये स हैहयः । दत्तात्रेयात् परामृद्धिमवाप्यातिबलान्वितः ॥

āghoṣayāmāsa tadā sthito rājye sa haihayaḥ | dattātreyāt parāmṛddhimavāpyātibalānvitaḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 19.20–21, above.

19.22

Sanskrit

अद्यप्रभृति यः शस्त्रं मामृते ऽन्यो ग्रहीष्यति । हन्तव्यः स मया दस्युः परिहंसारतो ऽपि वा ॥

adyaprabhṛti yaḥ śastraṃ māmṛte 'nyo grahīṣyati | hantavyaḥ sa mayā dasyuḥ parihaṃsārato 'pi vā ||

English

"From this day forth, whoever other than me will take up a weapon, that man is to be killed by me, whether he is a bandit49 or even one intent on injuring50."51

19.23

Sanskrit

इत्याज्ञप्तेन तद्राष्ट्रे कश्चिदायुधधृङ्नरः । तमृते पुरुषव्याघ्रं बभूवोरुपराक्रमः ॥

ityājñaptena tadrāṣṭre kaścidāyudhadhṛṅnaraḥ | tamṛte puruṣavyāghraṃ babhūvoruparākramaḥ ||

English

With the order thus given, in that realm there was [no] man of great prowess who bore a weapon, except him, the tiger among men.52

19.24

Sanskrit

स एव ग्रामपालो ऽभूत् पशुपालः स एव च । क्षेत्रपालः स एवासीद् द्विजातीनाञ्च रक्षिता ॥

sa eva grāmapālo 'bhūt paśupālaḥ sa eva ca | kṣetrapālaḥ sa evāsīd dvijātīnāñca rakṣitā ||

English

He alone became the protector of the villages, and he alone the protector of the herds. He alone was the protector of the fields, and he was the guardian of the twice-born53.54

19.25

Sanskrit

तपस्विनां पालयिता सार्थपालस्तु सो ऽभवत् । द्स्युव्यालाग्रिशस्त्रादिभयेष्वब्धौ निमज्जताम् ॥

tapasvināṃ pālayitā sārthapālastu so 'bhavat | dsyuvyālāgriśastrādibhayeṣvabdhau nimajjatām ||

English

19.25–26He became the protector of ascetics and the protector of caravans55 (sārtha); and for men sinking in the ocean amid fears of bandits, beasts56, fire, weapons and the like, and for men immersed in other calamities, that slayer of enemy heroes57, as soon as he was remembered, at once became the rescuer.58

19.26

Sanskrit

अन्यासु चैव मग्रानामापत्सु परवीरहा । स एव संस्मृतः सद्यः समुद्धर्ताभवन्नृणाम् ॥

anyāsu caiva magrānāmāpatsu paravīrahā | sa eva saṃsmṛtaḥ sadyaḥ samuddhartābhavannṛṇām ||

English

Its English is given with 19.25–26, above.

19.27

Sanskrit

अनष्टद्रव्यता चासीत् तस्मिन् शासति पार्थिवे । तेनेष्टं बहुभिर्यज्ञैः समाप्तवरदक्षिणैः ॥

anaṣṭadravyatā cāsīt tasmin śāsati pārthive | teneṣṭaṃ bahubhiryajñaiḥ samāptavaradakṣiṇaiḥ ||

English

While that king ruled, there was no loss of property, and he performed sacrifices, many of them, with excellent dakṣiṇās59 given in full.60

19.28

Sanskrit

तेनैव च तपस्तप्तं संग्रामेष्वभिचेष्टितम् । तस्यार्धिमतिमानञ्च दृष्ट्वा प्राहाङ्गिरा मुनिः ॥

tenaiva ca tapastaptaṃ saṃgrāmeṣvabhiceṣṭitam | tasyārdhimatimānañca dṛṣṭvā prāhāṅgirā muniḥ ||

English

By him alone tapas61 was practised, and exploits were performed in battles. Seeing his prosperity and his surpassing greatness, the sage Aṅgiras62 spoke.63

19.29

Sanskrit

न नूनं कार्तवीर्यस्य गतिं यास्यन्ति पार्थिवाः । यज्ञैर्दानैस्तपोभिर्वा संग्रामे चातिचेष्चितैः ॥

na nūnaṃ kārtavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti pārthivāḥ | yajñairdānaistapobhirvā saṃgrāme cāticeṣcitaiḥ ||

English

Surely no [other] kings will attain the state of64 Kārtavīrya, whether by sacrifices, by gifts, by tapas, or by exploits in battle.65

19.30

Sanskrit

दत्तात्रेयाद्दिन् यस्मिन् स प्रापर्धि नरेश्वरः । तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् दिने यागं दत्तात्रेयस्य सो ऽकरोत् ॥

dattātreyāddin yasmin sa prāpardhi nareśvaraḥ | tasmiṃstasmin dine yāgaṃ dattātreyasya so 'karot ||

English

On whatever day that lord of men obtained prosperity from Dattātreya, on each such day he performed the sacrifice of Dattātreya66.67

19.31

Sanskrit

तत्रैव च प्रजाः सर्वास्तस्मिन्नहनि भूपतेः । तस्यर्धि परमां दृष्ट्वा यागं चक्रुः समाधिना ॥

tatraiva ca prajāḥ sarvāstasminnahani bhūpateḥ | tasyardhi paramāṃ dṛṣṭvā yāgaṃ cakruḥ samādhinā ||

English

And in the same way all the subjects, on that day of the king68, seeing his supreme prosperity, performed the sacrifice69 with focused devotion.70

19.32

Sanskrit

इत्येतत् तस्य माहात्म्यं दत्तात्रेयस्य धीमतः । विष्णोश्चराचरगुरोरनन्तस्य महात्मनः ॥

ityetat tasya māhātmyaṃ dattātreyasya dhīmataḥ | viṣṇoścarācaraguroranantasya mahātmanaḥ ||

English

19.32–33Such is the greatness of him, of the wise Dattātreya, of Viṣṇu71, the teacher of the moving and the unmoving, the infinite, the great-souled. The manifestations72 of the bearer of the Śārṅga bow73, the infinite, the immeasurable, the bearer of conch, discus and mace, are told in the Purāṇas.74

19.33

Sanskrit

प्रादुर्भावाः पुराणेषु कथ्यन्ते शार्ड्गधन्विनः । अनन्तस्याप्रमेयस्य शङ्खचक्रगदाभृतः ॥

prādurbhāvāḥ purāṇeṣu kathyante śārḍgadhanvinaḥ | anantasyāprameyasya śaṅkhacakragadābhṛtaḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 19.32–33, above.

19.34

Sanskrit

एतस्य परमं रूपं यश्चिन्तयति मानवः । स सुखी स च संसारात् समुत्तीर्णो ऽचिराद्भवेत् ॥

etasya paramaṃ rūpaṃ yaścintayati mānavaḥ | sa sukhī sa ca saṃsārāt samuttīrṇo 'cirādbhavet ||

English

The man who meditates on the supreme form of this [Viṣṇu]75 will be happy, and before long he will have crossed over beyond saṃsāra76.77

19.35

Sanskrit

सदैव वैष्णवानाञ्च भक्त्याहं सुलभो ऽस्मि भोः । इत्येवं यस्य वै वाचस्तं कथं नाश्रयेज्जनः ॥

sadaiva vaiṣṇavānāñca bhaktyāhaṃ sulabho 'smi bhoḥ | ityevaṃ yasya vai vācastaṃ kathaṃ nāśrayejjanaḥ ||

English

[He] whose words are thus78: "And I am always easy to reach through the devotion of the Vaiṣṇavas79, O you!" — how would a person not take refuge in him?80

19.36

Sanskrit

अधर्मस्य विनाशाय धर्माचारार्थमेव च । अनादिनिधनो देवः करोति स्थितिपालनम् ॥

adharmasya vināśāya dharmācārārthameva ca | anādinidhano devaḥ karoti sthitipālanam ||

English

For the destruction of adharma and for the sake of the practice of dharma81, the god, who has neither beginning nor end82, carries out the preservation of the world order83.84

19.37

Sanskrit

तथैव जन्म चाख्यातमलर्कं कथयामि ते । तथा च योगः कथितो दत्तात्रेयेण तस्य वै । पितृभक्तस्य राजर्षेरलर्कस्य महात्मनः ॥

tathaiva janma cākhyātamalarkaṃ kathayāmi te | tathā ca yogaḥ kathito dattātreyeṇa tasya vai | pitṛbhaktasya rājarṣeralarkasya mahātmanaḥ ||

English

Likewise [Alarka's] birth has been told, and I tell you of Alarka85. And likewise the yoga86 was indeed declared by Dattātreya to him87, to Alarka, the royal sage devoted to his father, the great-souled.88

Sanskrit

इति श्रीमार्कण्डेयपुराणे दत्तात्रेयीये ऊनविंशो ऽध्यायः

iti śrīmārkaṇḍeyapurāṇe dattātreyīye ūnaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ

English

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, the Dattātreya section89, in the venerable90 Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa.91

  1. The reading: The line is only a chapter heading (ekonaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ, 'the nineteenth chapter'). The verse number 81.1 and the neighbouring references (80.15, 81.2) come from the e-text's own numbering and do not match the chapter number; I translate the heading as it stands. ↩
  2. the sage's words: The sage is Garga; the next verse (19.6) calls them 'Garga's words'. They are the advice at the end of the preceding chapter to worship Dattātreya. ↩
  3. Kārtavīrya: Kārtavīrya Arjuna, the Haihaya king, son of Kṛtavīrya. He is called Arjuna in the verses that follow. ↩
  4. in just the way the gods were told long ago: Refers to what Dattātreya had said earlier to the gods in the story of the preceding chapter (18.55-57), where he is approached by them. ↩
  5. The reading: (1) bhūtaṃ in 19.3 gives no good sense as a participle ('who was there'). I take it as a corruption of bhaktam ('devoted') and translate 'the devotee'; bhūtvā is another possible correction, but it would leave tam without a noun to agree with. (2) 19.4-19.5 is probably corrupt or elliptical. kutsitam is neuter and cannot agree with aham, so 'I am always [so]' (sadaivāhaṃ) is a supplied sense: I am always engaged in such enjoyment. aham is rendered, and the bracketed word marks the gap. (3) aśaktam is taken, as the reviewer says, with mām ('me, who am unable [to help]') as the object of uparoddhum. I have therefore removed my earlier bracketed 'not', which the Sanskrit does not have before ārādhayasva. (4) gandhāmbu is read as two items, 'perfumes, water', not 'perfumed water'. (5) yathaiva ... tathaiva is rendered as a correlation: he spoke to him just as the gods had been told, and the blame of liquor and the like is the content of what was said. (6) strī ceyaṃ mama pārśvasthā ity eta ↩
  6. that saying of Garga: The words of the sage Garga, mentioned in the preceding verses, which sent the king to Dattātreya. ↩
  7. Sārtavīrya Arjuna: The text reads sārtavīryārjuna, evidently for Kārtavīryārjuna: the Haihaya king Arjuna Kārtavīrya, already called Kārtavīrya in 19.1. ↩
  8. The reading: The reading sārtavīryārjunaḥ is probably a corruption or variant of kārtavīryārjunaḥ. I kept the text's form in the translation and treated it as the same person as Kārtavīrya. The speaker's name jaḍa is read as the narrator; the preceding 'putra uvāca' and the following 'arjuna uvāca' are separate frames not translated here. ↩
  9. māyā: Here the power of illusion or deceptive appearance by which a god veils his true nature. Arjuna means that Dattātreya's show of drinking and keeping a woman at his side is a pretence. ↩
  10. the source of all existence: Sanskrit sarvabhavāraṇiḥ, literally 'the fire-stick (araṇi) of all beings/existence'. The araṇi is the wooden piece rubbed to kindle fire, so the goddess is the generating source of all that exists. Taken here as an epithet of the goddess (devī). ↩
  11. The reading: The reference '81.9' is evidently a misnumbering of the speaker's line 'arjuna uvāca', which belongs just before 19.7; I translated it as the speaker's line. 'tathaiva' ('and so too') is rendered 'and so is this goddess'. 'sarvabhavāraṇiḥ' could also be read as 'the araṇi of all that is born' (bhava as birth), but the sense of source is the same. 'anagha' is taken as a predicate ('You are sinless') rather than as a vocative, since it stands with 'tvam' and is paralleled by 'iyaṃ devī'. ↩
  12. the god: Dattātreya, the sage-deity whom Kārtavīrya has approached. The verse itself says only deva, 'the god'. ↩
  13. greatly fortunate: mahābhāga: 'of great fortune', 'illustrious'. An epithet of Kārtavīrya. ↩
  14. The reading: Finding 1 accepted: ityuktaḥ and prītimān both agree with devaḥ, so the sentence now reads 'Thus addressed, the god, pleased, then replied'. Finding 2 accepted: vaśīkṛta is rendered 'subjugated' and mahītala 'the surface of the earth'. The particle ha is emphatic and left untranslated. tam and kārtavīryam are in apposition ('to him, to Kārtavīrya'), and both are now rendered. The verse does not name Dattātreya; 'the god' is identified with him from context. ↩
  15. My secret, which has been declared aloud by you: Refers to Arjuna's words in 19.7. By saying that the god is sinless and is using his own māyā to bewilder him, Arjuna has seen through the god's pretence of enjoying wine and a woman, which the god had presented as a fault. ↩
  16. The reading: guhyaṃ me yat tvayā samudīritam: me can be a genitive with guhyam ('my secret') or a dative ('to me'). The reviewer is right that the draft's 'disclosed to me' contradicted its own note. I now take me as a genitive with guhyam throughout, since the secret is the god's own concealed nature, which Arjuna has declared. The mama later in the verse is kept separate, as 'in me'. tena is now rendered once, as 'by that', picking up the relative clause. I kept 'O king' for pārthiva, as the reviewer allows, because it is a common word and needs no note. ↩
  17. ghee: ghee (ājya) is clarified butter, used in food and in ritual offerings. ↩
  18. The reading: The sentence continues into 19.11 (lakṣmīsametaṃ, gītaiś ca, etc.) and the main verb comes in 19.12 (pradāsyāmi). Here only the opening relative clause is translated, ending in a comma. Also, 'ājya' is rendered 'ghee', an English word that is not given in the glossary. miṣṭānnaiḥ is read as 'sweet foods', not 'sweetened rice'. The ' //' is omitted because the sentence is unfinished. ↩
  19. Lakṣmī: The goddess of fortune and prosperity, here the consort who accompanies the god (Dattātreya). ↩
  20. brāhmaṇas: Members of the priestly, learned class; honouring them is a standard pious act. ↩
  21. lute: The text reads voṇā, which is vīṇā, a stringed instrument. ↩
  22. The reading: lakṣmīsametam is accusative singular and so agrees with the māṃ ('me') of 19.10. I took it as 'me, accompanied by Lakṣmī'. The sentence has no verb here; it continues from 19.10 (ye ... māṃ pūjayiṣyanti) and resolves at teṣām in 19.12, so I supplied 'those men who will worship' in brackets. voṇā is read as vīṇā (lute). ↩
  23. the assault of those who scorn [them]: The verse is the main clause of a sentence begun in 19.10–11 ("those men who will worship me..."). Both teṣām and avamanyatām refer to those worshippers. avamanyatām is the genitive plural of the present participle, "of those who scorn". ↩
  24. The reading: avaghāta can mean a blow, injury or killing. avamanyatām ("of those who scorn") could depend on avaghātam ("the assault of the scorners") or be the object of haniṣyāmi ("I shall strike down those who scorn"). I chose the first: avaghāta is the harm the scorners would do to the worshippers, and the god destroys it. The 'those who scorn' are taken to be scorners of the worshippers, not of the god. putradāradhanādikam is neuter singular and in apposition to tuṣṭim; I render it as "[together with] sons, wife, wealth and the like". ↩
  25. choose a boon: varaya is not the regular middle imperative vṛṇīṣva, which verse 19.9 uses. It is an irregular active imperative of vṛ, 'to choose', and means the same. ↩
  26. desire in [your] mind: The text reads yanmasepsitam, which is a misprint. It is read here as yan manasepsitam, that is yat manasā īpsitam, 'what is desired by the mind'. The bracketed 'your' is implied by te. ↩
  27. my secret name: This refers back to the secret that Kārtavīrya declared aloud (verse 19.9: guhyaṃ me yat tvayā samudīritam). The verses given do not say what name he spoke. ↩
  28. The reading: 1. yanmasepsitam is evidently corrupt. I accept the reviewer's reading yan manasepsitam (manasā īpsitam, 'desired by the mind'). It is the smallest change and keeps the instrumental, which my earlier draft dropped. My earlier 'desired by you' was only a guess, and I withdraw it. 'In [your] mind' is bracketed because te only implies the possessor. The reading is an emendation, and the note says so. 2. sa tvam is taken as 'so you', resuming the address. 3. prasādasumukhaḥ is rendered 'graciously well disposed'. Sumukha means 'fair-faced' or 'well disposed', and prasāda means grace or favour. I dropped my earlier note, which glossed it loosely as 'face made kind'. 4. guhyanāmaprakīrtanāt is an ablative of cause, 'because of the proclaiming of the secret name'. Since 19.7 contains no name, the note stays cautious about what the name was. ↩
  29. adharma: The opposite of dharma: unrighteousness, wrongful conduct, and the demerit that follows from it. Here it means the fault a king might incur in ruling. ↩
  30. The reading: The reference "81.17" is a numbering error in the e-text for what is, in effect, the speaker's line introducing 19.14. I treated it as the speaker's line. In 19.14, ṛddhi could mean prosperity, success or accomplishment; I chose "prosperity" because the next verses ask for specific powers. The text reads "prayacchardhim", which I resolved as prayaccha + ṛddhim. The form "avāpnuyām" is an optative: "may I incur". ↩
  31. knowledge in tracking down others: parānusaraṇe jñānam: literally 'knowledge in following after others'. It is commonly understood as the ability to find out or pursue others, such as enemies or fugitives; the sense is not fully fixed. ↩
  32. lightness: laghutā: lightness or nimbleness, here the ease and speed with which the arms act. ↩
  33. The reading: parānusaraṇe jñānam can mean 'knowledge of tracking others' (the power to find or pursue foes) or 'knowledge when following others'. I chose the first as the more natural in a warrior's request. laghutāguṇam is a compound qualifying sahasram bāhūnām: 'a thousand arms having the quality of lightness'. I supply 'in wielding' in brackets only for the English to parse; the Sanskrit gives only 'the quality of lightness'. ↩
  34. nether worlds: pātāla: the subterranean realms beneath the earth, traditionally seven in number. ↩
  35. may my death come from a man who is superior [to me]: Literally 'and death from a superior man'. The ablative narāt gives the agent of the killing. The words 'to me' are implied by the comparative sense of adhika. ↩
  36. The reading: The verse has no verb for the second clause, so 'may my death come' is supplied from 'santu' and 'asaṅgā gatayaḥ'. Adhikāt could also mean 'from one greater' in a general sense, but I read it as 'superior to me'. The bracketed 'to me' is implied. ↩
  37. for one who has set out on a wrong path: The text reads tathonmārgapravṛttasya, that is tathā + unmārgapravṛttasya, with the sandhi ā + u > o. It is a genitive, 'of one set out on a wrong path', construed with sanmārgadeśakaḥ, 'one who shows the good path'. ↩
  38. in the giving of wealth and likewise in [its] inexhaustibility: Vittadāne and akṣaye are parallel locatives, 'in the giving of wealth' and 'in inexhaustibility'. Both qualify the guests (ślāghyāḥ), and 'its' is understood from vitta. Verse 19.18 goes on to ask that wealth not be lost. ↩
  39. The reading: (1) Unmārgapravṛttasya has no explicit referent. It may mean any person who strays, or Kārtavīrya himself. The surrounding wishes are all for himself, so the second sense is likely, but I kept the literal 'one who has set out on a wrong path' and did not add 'me'. (2) Akṣaye: I accept the reviewer's correction. Akṣaya is the negation of kṣaya and means 'imperishability, inexhaustibility', not 'exhaustion', and it fits 19.18 (anaṣṭadravyatā). The earlier alternative reading 'exhaustion' is withdrawn. (3) Ślāghyā is taken with atithayaḥ, and 'its' is supplied from vitta. ↩
  40. through remembrance of me: The instrumental anusmaraṇena is taken as the cause: property is not lost because of people's remembering the speaker. The verse states no further effect. ↩
  41. devotion: bhakti: loving devotion and faithful attachment to a deity. Here it is Kārtavīrya's devotion to the god he addresses, Dattātreya, who is granting the boons. ↩
  42. The reading: mamānusmaraṇena ca: the construction is compressed, and I supply no verb. I take the instrumental as the cause of the first phrase, so that property is not lost through remembrance of me, and I no longer supply 'recovered' as in my draft. Mama could also go with rāṣṭre ('in my kingdom'), leaving anusmaraṇena as a bare 'by remembrance'. I join it to anusmaraṇena, since that gives the natural sense 'remembrance of me'. I keep 'and' for ca rather than 'even'. In mamaiva I now keep the emphasis of eva as 'my own'. ↩
  43. cakravartin: A universal emperor, literally one whose wheel turns (everywhere unobstructed); the ideal sovereign over the whole earth. The text reads cakravarto, which is taken as a form of cakravartin. ↩
  44. The reading: Yatra te kīrtitāḥ: yatra is literally 'where' or 'in which'. It could mean 'in that [prayer]' or 'in the matter of which'. I took it as 'here', that is, in the request just made, so the sense is 'the boons you have named'. Cakravarto tvam īśvaraḥ: cakravarto is probably a corrupt or metrically shortened form of cakravartī. I read it as cakravartī and took īśvaraḥ as an appositive meaning 'sovereign lord'. The e-text also has the verse number 19.19 after 82.3, which looks like a numbering mix-up in the source. ↩
  45. prakṛtis: Here the constituent elements of the state or the subjects: ministers, officials and the people. The word can also mean the constituents of the kingdom (the seven prakṛtis); the sense here is the leading persons of the realm. ↩
  46. the consecration: abhiṣeka, the ritual sprinkling by which a king is installed. ↩
  47. Haihaya: Arjuna (Kārtavīrya) belonged to the Haihaya people, so the name serves as a patronymic-type epithet for him. ↩
  48. The reading: prakṛtīḥ: either 'subjects' (the people) or 'ministers/constituents of the state'. I kept the word in IAST with a note, since the sense covers both. ānāyya is read as 'having summoned', with Arjuna as the agent. ↩
  49. bandit: dasyu: robber, outlaw, enemy of order. ↩
  50. intent on injuring: The printed parihaṃsārataḥ is probably a corruption of parihiṃsārataḥ, 'intent on injury', which is the reading translated. Another possible emendation is parihāsa-, 'sport, jest'. ↩
  51. The reading: parihaṃsārataḥ: the printed parihaṃsā- is not a regular word. Two emendations are possible: parihiṃsā- ('injury'), giving 'intent on injuring', or parihāsa- ('jest, sport'), giving 'fond of sport', that is, one who takes up weapons even in play. I keep parihiṃsā-: it is the smaller change from the print and suits a proclamation against violence. Accepted from the reviewer: dasyuḥ and parihaṃsārataḥ are both nominatives in apposition to sa, so the rendering is now 'whether he is a bandit or even one intent on injuring', with one victim and two possible descriptions. The future 'will take up' now renders grahīṣyati. The dasyu note no longer says that every weapon-taker is a dasyu. Not accepted: marking the emendation with a bracket in the translation. Square brackets are reserved for words the Sanskrit implies but does not say, so they cannot flag a textual choice. The emendation is flagged in the note and here instead. I keep the quotation marks because the verse gives the content of th ↩
  52. The reading: 1) The text as printed has no negative, which would make the verse say that weapon-bearers did exist besides Arjuna. The context (19.22 and 19.24, 'he alone became the village-protector...') requires 'no one but him', so I supply [no], assuming na has dropped out (perhaps kaścid for na kaścid). 2) ityājñaptena is an instrumental, 'by him/that which was thus ordered'. I take it as an absolute-type phrase, 'with the order thus given'; ityājñapte (locative absolute) may have been intended. 3) uruparākramaḥ is nominative, so I take it with naraḥ, 'a man of great prowess', rather than with the accusative puruṣavyāghram; it could also be read as a description of Arjuna (babhūva, 'he became mighty'), but then the nominative would not agree with the accusative. ↩
  53. twice-born: dvijāti (dvija): the three upper classes (brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas), who undergo the second birth of initiation. ↩
  54. The reading: The text reads dvijātīnāñca (a printed form of dvijātīnāṃ ca). The Sanskrit has 'ca' joining the last clause, which I render with 'and'. The sentence is 'sa eva' repeated three times; I kept the repetition as 'he alone'. ↩
  55. caravans: sārtha is a company of merchants or travellers moving together, usually with goods and an armed escort. The sārthapāla guards such a company on the road. ↩
  56. beasts: vyāla can mean a beast of prey or a snake. Both fit the list of dangers. ↩
  57. that slayer of enemy heroes: paravīrahā is a stock epithet of warrior kings. It qualifies the same Arjuna (the Haihaya king) who is the subject throughout. ↩
  58. The reading: 1) The text prints 'dsyu-', evidently a misprint for dasyu-; I read dasyu ('bandit'). 2) abdhau nimajjatām: 'ocean' may be literal (men sinking at sea, with sea-dangers included in the list) or a metaphor for the fears named next. I kept 'in the ocean amid fears of...', which allows either. 3) vyāla: 'beasts' or 'snakes'; I chose 'beasts' as the general sense. 4) Reading of 'sa eva' as the king (Arjuna) follows 19.24; saṃsmṛtaḥ is rendered 'as soon as he was remembered'. ↩
  59. dakṣiṇās: The fees or gifts given to the priests who officiate at a sacrifice, required for its completion. ↩
  60. The reading: anaṣṭadravyatā is an abstract noun, 'the state of having no lost goods'. I rendered it as 'no loss of property', and read 'tasmin śāsati pārthive' as a locative absolute, 'while that king ruled'. The verb in the second half is impersonal passive: iṣṭam with instrumental teṇa, 'was sacrificed by him'. I rendered it actively. 'Yajñaiḥ' is an instrumental of means with iṣṭam, so 'performed sacrifices' is a fair sense. Samāpta-vara-dakṣiṇaiḥ is a bahuvrīhi, 'with excellent fees completed/fully given', which I read as describing the sacrifices. ↩
  61. tapas: Austerity or ascetic discipline, understood as a store of spiritual power. Here it is attributed to a king. ↩
  62. Aṅgiras: A Vedic seer. The text has Aṅgirā, the nominative of the stem Aṅgiras. His speech follows in 19.29. ↩
  63. The reading: The compound tasyārdhimatimānam is unclear. 'ardhi' is read as ṛddhi, 'prosperity'. 'atimānam' is taken as ati-māna, 'surpassing measure' or 'greatness'. Other readings are 'excessive pride', or an emendation to ṛddhim atimānuṣīm, 'superhuman prosperity'. I kept the transmitted reading and translated it as 'surpassing greatness'. 'Pride' seems unlikely for a sage's admiring comment. The subject of 'tenaiva' is not named in this verse. It is the same king as in 19.27, and 19.29 names him Kārtavīrya. ↩
  64. attain the state of: gatiṃ yā- means literally 'go to the course or goal of'; it is read here as 'reach the position or attainment of', i.e. equal his standing. ↩
  65. The reading: The text has 'cāticeṣcitaiḥ', which is a misprint for 'cāticeṣṭitaiḥ' (ati-ceṣṭita, 'surpassing deeds, exploits'). I read it so. 'nūnam' may be 'surely' (assertion) or 'indeed/certainly not'; I took it as 'surely'. The word 'other' in brackets is implied by the comparison with Kārtavīrya, but pārthivāḥ could also simply mean 'kings' in general. ↩
  66. the sacrifice of Dattātreya: The genitive dattātreyasya is read as 'in honour of, addressed to Dattātreya'. The word is yāga, a synonym of yajña, here a rite of worship. ↩
  67. The reading: The printed text 'dattātreyāddin yasmin' and 'prāpardhi' looks corrupt or misprinted. I read dattātreyād dine yasmin and prāpa ṛddhim (prāpardhim), 'on whatever day he obtained prosperity from Dattātreya'. A literal reading of the e-text is impossible, and this emendation fits the sense and the following verses (19.31, on ṛddhi and the yāga). ↩
  68. on that day of the king: bhūpateḥ is taken with tasmin ahani: the day belonging to the king, that is, the day on which he obtained prosperity from Dattātreya (19.30). ↩
  69. performed the sacrifice: The yāga is that of Dattātreya, which Kārtavīrya performed on the day he obtained prosperity (19.30). His subjects now follow his example and keep the same rite on that day. ↩
  70. The reading: tatra eva: the draft's local 'in that very place' is dropped. No place has been named, so the reviewer is right on this point and I take 'in the same way, likewise', after the king's own practice in 19.30. A reference to his realm, 'in that very [kingdom]', is grammatically possible but unsupported. bhūpateḥ: the reviewer proposes 'on that day, seeing the supreme prosperity of the king'. I keep bhūpateḥ with ahani ('that day of the king'), since tasya already supplies the king in tasya ṛddhim. Taking it with ṛddhim in apposition to tasya is a possible alternative reading, and the sense is nearly the same. samādhinā: the instrumental singular names the manner of the act, so I now render 'with focused devotion' instead of 'with concentrated minds'. The annual recurrence suggested by the reviewer is not stated. The distributive tasmin tasmin dine in 19.30 only implies that the rite is performed on that day whenever it comes, so the note does not say 'annual'. ↩
  71. of Viṣṇu: The genitives in 19.32 (Dattātreya, Viṣṇu, the infinite, the great-souled) stand in apposition, so the verse identifies Dattātreya with Viṣṇu. ↩
  72. manifestations: prādurbhāva: appearance or manifestation of a deity in the world, used of Viṣṇu's descents (avatāras). Dattātreya is here reckoned one of them. ↩
  73. the Śārṅga bow: Śārṅga (printed śārḍga in the text) is the name of Viṣṇu's bow. Śārṅgadhanvin, 'bearer of the Śārṅga bow', is an epithet of Viṣṇu. ↩
  74. The reading: The text prints śārḍgadhanvinaḥ for śārṅgadhanvinaḥ, probably a misprint; I read Śārṅga. The genitives in 19.32 could be read as naming Dattātreya and Viṣṇu as two persons. I took them as one person in apposition because every genitive agrees with the same subject and 19.33 then speaks of Viṣṇu's manifestations. ↩
  75. this [Viṣṇu]: etasya refers back to the god of the preceding verses, Viṣṇu, who is identified with Dattātreya. ↩
  76. saṃsāra: The cycle of birth, death and rebirth; the round of worldly existence. ↩
  77. The reading: etasya has no named referent in this verse. I take it to be Viṣṇu (Dattātreya) from 19.32–33. Bhavet is optative; I render it as a future ('will be') because it states a promised result. ↩
  78. [He] whose words are thus: The relative clause yasya vācaḥ ('whose words') is answered by taṃ ('him'); the speaker quoted is the Lord, Viṣṇu, who is identified with Dattātreya in this passage. ↩
  79. Vaiṣṇavas: Vaiṣṇava: a devotee of Viṣṇu. ↩
  80. The reading: vaiṣṇavānām (genitive plural) can be taken with bhaktyā ('through the devotion of the Vaiṣṇavas') or with sulabhaḥ ('easy for the Vaiṣṇavas to reach, through devotion'). I chose the first, since it follows the word order and a genitive of the devotee with bhakti is natural. The particle ca ('and') links this verse loosely to the previous statement. The subject of nāśrayet, janaḥ, is rendered as 'a person'. ↩
  81. dharma: Righteousness, right conduct and the established moral order; the counterpart of adharma. ↩
  82. who has neither beginning nor end: anādinidhana: literally 'without beginning and death/end'. The god is identified with Viṣṇu, as in the preceding verses. ↩
  83. the preservation of the world order: sthitipālanam: literally 'the protecting of what stands (sthiti)', that is, the maintenance of the existing order of the world. Here it names the god's function of preserving the world, in contrast to its creation and dissolution. ↩
  84. The reading: dharmācārārtham: read as 'for the sake of the practice (ācāra) of dharma', a tatpuruṣa. An alternative is 'for the sake of conduct according to dharma'; the difference is slight. sthitipālanam: 'preservation of the world order' is chosen; 'protection of what exists' or 'upholding of stability' are also possible. ↩
  85. I tell you of Alarka: The accusative alarkam is irregular. It may be a corruption of alarkasya, 'the birth of Alarka'. As printed it is the object of kathayāmi. ↩
  86. yoga: Discipline of mind and body aimed at union with, or knowledge of, the supreme; here the teaching on it that Dattātreya gave to Alarka. ↩
  87. to him: tasya is a genitive used for a dative. It stands in apposition with the genitives pitṛbhaktasya, rājarṣeḥ, alarkasya and mahātmanaḥ, which all name the same man, so 'his yoga' is not intended. ↩
  88. The reading: (1) 'alarkaṃ': the accusative may be corrupt for 'alarkasya' (so 'the birth of Alarka has been told to you'). I keep the printed text, with 'janma' as subject of 'ākhyātam' and 'alarkam' as object of 'kathayāmi', and flag the problem in a note. I supply '[Alarka's]' in brackets because the birth is evidently his. (2) 'tasya': it is not 'his yoga', because it is resumed by the appositive genitives 'alarkasya' etc., so I read 'to him, to Alarka'. (3) 'vai' is rendered 'indeed'. ↩
  89. the Dattātreya section: Sanskrit dattātreyīye, 'concerning Dattātreya': the name of the group of chapters in this Purāṇa that deal with Dattātreya. It is a locative form agreeing with 'Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa' in the colophon formula. ↩
  90. venerable: Sanskrit śrī-, an honorific prefix customary in titles and colophons. ↩
  91. The reading: dattātreyīye is taken as a locative qualifying the Purāṇa, meaning 'in the Dattātreya section'. It could also be read as the name of a sub-collection of chapters within the Purāṇa. The sense is the same either way. ↩

Adhyāya 20

Sanskrit

विंशो ऽध्यायः

viṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ

English

The twentieth chapter.

Sanskrit

जड उवाच

jaḍa uvāca

20.1

Sanskrit

प्राग्बभूव महावीर्यः शत्रुजिन्नाम पार्थिवः । तुतोष यस्य यज्ञेषु सोमावाप्त्या पुरन्दरः ॥

prāgbabhūva mahāvīryaḥ śatrujinnāma pārthivaḥ | tutoṣa yasya yajñeṣu somāvāptyā purandaraḥ ||

English

In former times there was a king named Śatrujit1, of great valour, in whose yajñas Purandara2 was gratified at receiving soma3.4

20.2

Sanskrit

तस्यात्मजो महावीर्यो बभूवारिविदारणः । बुद्धिविक्रमलावण्यैर्गुरुशक्राश्विभिः समः ॥

tasyātmajo mahāvīryo babhūvārividāraṇaḥ | buddhivikramalāvaṇyairguruśakrāśvibhiḥ samaḥ ||

English

His son was born, of great valour, a tearer of enemies, equal to Guru5, Śakra6 and the Aśvins7 in intelligence, prowess and beauty.8

20.3

Sanskrit

स समानवयोबुद्धिसत्त्वविक्रमचेष्टितैः । नृपपुत्रो नृपसुतैर्नित्यमास्ते समावृतः ॥

sa samānavayobuddhisattvavikramaceṣṭitaiḥ | nṛpaputro nṛpasutairnityamāste samāvṛtaḥ ||

English

That king's son was always surrounded by other princes, sons of kings, who were equal to him in age, intelligence, courage, prowess and conduct.9†

20.4

Sanskrit

कदाचिच्छास्त्रसम्भारविवेककृतनिश्चयः । कदाचित् काव्यसंलापगीतनाटकसम्भवैः ॥

kadācicchāstrasambhāravivekakṛtaniścayaḥ | kadācit kāvyasaṃlāpagītanāṭakasambhavaiḥ ||

English

20.4–6Sometimes reaching firm conclusions by discerning among the mass of treatises10, sometimes in the pleasures arising from poetry, conversation, song and drama, and likewise in diversions with dice and in the suitable [exercises]11 in the training in weapons and missiles12, and intent on practice with war elephants, horses and chariots, that son of the king sported with the sons of kings. As by day, so also by night he was filled with joy.13

20.5

Sanskrit

तथैवाक्षविनोदैश्च शस्त्रास्त्रविनयेषु च । योग्यानि युद्धनागाश्वस्यन्दनाभ्यासतत्परः ॥

tathaivākṣavinodaiśca śastrāstravinayeṣu ca | yogyāni yuddhanāgāśvasyandanābhyāsatatparaḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 20.4–6, above.

20.6

Sanskrit

रेमे नरेन्द्रपुत्रो ऽसौ नरेन्द्रतनयैः सह । यथैव हि दिवा तद्वद्रात्रवपि मुदा युतः ॥

reme narendraputro 'sau narendratanayaiḥ saha | yathaiva hi divā tadvadrātravapi mudā yutaḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 20.4–6, above.

20.7

Sanskrit

तेषां तु क्रीडतां तत्र द्विजभूपविशां सुताः । समानवयसः प्रीत्या रन्तुमायान्त्यनेकशः ॥

teṣāṃ tu krīḍatāṃ tatra dvijabhūpaviśāṃ sutāḥ | samānavayasaḥ prītyā rantumāyāntyanekaśaḥ ||

English

As they played there, the sons of brahmins, kings and commoners14, of the same age as they, came again and again to play with them in affection.15

20.8

Sanskrit

कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य नागलोकान्महीतलम् । कुमारावागतौ नागौ पुत्रावश्वतरस्य तु ॥

kasyacittvatha kālasya nāgalokānmahītalam | kumārāvāgatau nāgau putrāvaśvatarasya tu ||

English

20.8–10Then, after some time, two young nāgas16, the sons of Aśvatara17, came from the world of the nāgas to the surface of the earth. Disguised in the form of brahmins, young and pleasing to look at, the two stayed there with those king's sons, and likewise with other twice-born18, joined with them in affection in various diversions. And all those king's sons, and those sons of brahmins and commoners,19

20.9

Sanskrit

ब्रह्मरूपप्रतिच्छन्नौ तरुणौ प्रियदर्शनौ । तौ तैर्नृपसुतैः सार्धं तथैवान्यैर्द्विजन्मभिः ॥

brahmarūpapraticchannau taruṇau priyadarśanau | tau tairnṛpasutaiḥ sārdhaṃ tathaivānyairdvijanmabhiḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 20.8–10, above.

20.10

Sanskrit

विनोदैर्विविधैस्तत्र तस्थतुः प्रीतिसंयुतौ । सर्व च ते नृपसुतास्ते च ब्रह्मविशां सुताः ॥

vinodairvividhaistatra tasthatuḥ prītisaṃyutau | sarva ca te nṛpasutāste ca brahmaviśāṃ sutāḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 20.8–10, above.

20.11

Sanskrit

नागराजात्मजौ तौ च स्त्रानसंवाहनादिकम् । वस्त्रगन्धानुसयुक्तां चक्रुर्भागभुजिक्रियाम् ॥

nāgarājātmajau tau ca strānasaṃvāhanādikam | vastragandhānusayuktāṃ cakrurbhāgabhujikriyām ||

English

And those two sons of the nāga king20, [with the others,] performed bathing, massage21 and the like, and the taking of meals in shares, accompanied by clothes and perfumes.22

20.12

Sanskrit

अहन्यहन्यनुप्राप्ते तौ च नागकुमारकौ । आजग्मतुर्मुदा युक्तौ प्रीत्या सूनोर्महीपतेः ॥

ahanyahanyanuprāpte tau ca nāgakumārakau | ājagmaturmudā yuktau prītyā sūnormahīpateḥ ||

English

As day after day came round, those two young nāgas too came, joined with joy, out of affection for the king's son23.24

20.13

Sanskrit

स च ताभ्यां नृपसुतः परं निर्वाणमाप्तवान् । विनोदैर्विविधैर्हास्यसंलापादिभिरेव च ॥

sa ca tābhyāṃ nṛpasutaḥ paraṃ nirvāṇamāptavān | vinodairvividhairhāsyasaṃlāpādibhireva ca ||

English

And that king's son, through those two, and through various diversions, jesting, conversation and the like, attained supreme peace25.26

20.14

Sanskrit

विना ताभ्यां न बुभुजे न सस्त्रौ न पपौ मधु । न रराम न जग्राह शास्त्राण्यात्मगुणर्धये ॥

vinā tābhyāṃ na bubhuje na sastrau na papau madhu | na rarāma na jagrāha śāstrāṇyātmaguṇardhaye ||

English

Without those two he would not eat, he would not bathe, he would not drink wine27, he took no pleasure, and he did not take up28 the śāstras for the increase of his own good qualities.29

20.15

Sanskrit

रसातले च तौ रात्रिं विना तेन महात्मना । निश्वासपरमौ नीत्वा जग्मतुस्तं दिने दिने ॥

rasātale ca tau rātriṃ vinā tena mahātmanā | niśvāsaparamau nītvā jagmatustaṃ dine dine ||

English

And in Rasātala30 the two, spending the night without that great-souled one and sighing deeply, would go to him day after day.31

20.16

Sanskrit

मर्त्यलोके परा प्रीतिर्भवतोः केन पुत्रकौ । सहेति पप्रच्छ पिता तावुभौ नागदारकौ ॥

martyaloke parā prītirbhavatoḥ kena putrakau | saheti papraccha pitā tāvubhau nāgadārakau ||

English

"In the world of mortals, with whom do you two have supreme affection, sons?" So the father32 asked both those young nāgas33.34

20.17

Sanskrit

दृष्टयोरत्र पाताले बहूनि दिवसानि मे । दिवा रजन्यामेवोभौ पश्यामि प्रियदर्शनौ ॥

dṛṣṭayoratra pātāle bahūni divasāni me | divā rajanyāmevobhau paśyāmi priyadarśanau ||

English

For many days, here in the nether worlds, you two have been unseen by me by day35; at night only I see you both, dear to look upon.36

Sanskrit

जड उवाच

jaḍa uvāca

20.18

Sanskrit

इति पित्रा स्वयं पृष्टौ प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जली । प्रत्यूचतुर्महाभागावुरगाधिपतेः सुतौ ॥

iti pitrā svayaṃ pṛṣṭau praṇipatya kṛtāñjalī | pratyūcaturmahābhāgāvuragādhipateḥ sutau ||

English

Thus questioned by their father himself, the two greatly fortunate sons of the lord of serpents37 bowed down, joined their palms in reverence38, and replied.39

Sanskrit

पुत्रावूचतुः

putrāvūcatuḥ

English

The two sons said:

20.19

Sanskrit

पुत्रः शत्रुजितस्तात नाम्ना ख्यात ऋतध्वजः । रूपवानार्जवोपेतः शूरो मानी प्रियंवदः ॥

putraḥ śatrujitastāta nāmnā khyāta ṛtadhvajaḥ | rūpavānārjavopetaḥ śūro mānī priyaṃvadaḥ ||

English

20.19–20Father, Śatrujit's son is famed by the name Ṛtadhvaja40: handsome, endowed with uprightness, a hero, self-respecting41, and sweet in speech; one who speaks only when asked, eloquent, learned, friendly, a mine of good qualities, one who honours those worthy of honour, wise, modest, and having discipline as his ornament42.

20.20

Sanskrit

अनापृष्टकथो वाग्ग्मी विद्वान् मैत्रो गुणाकरः । मान्यमानयिता धीमान् ह्रीमान् विनयभूषणः ॥

anāpṛṣṭakatho vāggmī vidvān maitro guṇākaraḥ | mānyamānayitā dhīmān hrīmān vinayabhūṣaṇaḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 20.19–20, above.

20.21

Sanskrit

तस्योपचारसम्प्रीतिसम्बोगापहृतं मनः । नागलोके भुवर्लोके न रतिं विन्दते पितः ॥

tasyopacārasamprītisambogāpahṛtaṃ manaḥ | nāgaloke bhuvarloke na ratiṃ vindate pitaḥ ||

English

Father, [our] mind, carried away by his courtesies, his affection and the enjoyment of his company43, finds no delight in the world of the nāgas or in the Bhuvarloka44.45

20.22

Sanskrit

तद्वियोगेन नस्तात ! न पातालञ्च शीतलम् । परितापाय तत्सङ्गादाह्लादाय रविर्दिवा ॥

tadviyogena nastāta ! na pātālañca śītalam | paritāpāya tatsaṅgādāhlādāya ravirdivā ||

English

Father, through separation from him the nether worlds are not cool to us, and are a source of torment; through union with him the sun by day is a source of delight.46

Sanskrit

पितोवाच

pitovāca

20.23

Sanskrit

पुत्रः पुण्यवतो धन्यः स यस्यैवं भविद्विधैः । परोक्षस्यापि गुणिभैः क्रियते गुणकीर्तनम् ॥

putraḥ puṇyavato dhanyaḥ sa yasyaivaṃ bhavidvidhaiḥ | parokṣasyāpi guṇibhaiḥ kriyate guṇakīrtanam ||

English

The son of a man of merit is fortunate, he whose good qualities are thus praised, even in his absence, by virtuous people such as you.47

20.24

Sanskrit

सन्ति शास्त्रविदो ऽशीलाः सन्ति मूर्खाः सुशीलिनः । शास्त्रशीले समं मन्ये पुत्रौ धन्यतरन्तु तम् ॥

santi śāstravido 'śīlāḥ santi mūrkhāḥ suśīlinaḥ | śāstraśīle samaṃ manye putrau dhanyatarantu tam ||

English

There are men learned in the śāstra who lack good conduct, and there are fools who have good conduct. Sons, I regard learning and good conduct as equal48, but I think him the more fortunate49.50†

20.25

Sanskrit

तस्य मित्रगुणान् मित्राण्यमित्राश्च पराक्रमम् । कथयन्ति सदा सत्सु पुत्रवांस्तेन वै पिता ॥

tasya mitraguṇān mitrāṇyamitrāśca parākramam | kathayanti sadā satsu putravāṃstena vai pitā ||

English

Friends speak of his qualities as a friend, and enemies of his valour, always in the company of good people; through him, indeed, a father is one who has a son.51

20.26

Sanskrit

तस्योपकारिणः कच्चिद् भवद्भ्यामभिवाञ्छितम् । किञ्चिन्निष्पादितं वत्सौ परितोषाय चेतसः ॥

tasyopakāriṇaḥ kaccid bhavadbhyāmabhivāñchitam | kiñcinniṣpāditaṃ vatsau paritoṣāya cetasaḥ ||

English

Has anything that he desired, children, been accomplished by the two of you for the satisfaction of the mind of that benefactor of yours?52

20.27

Sanskrit

स धन्यो जीवितं तस्य तस्य जन्म सुजन्मनः । यस्यार्थिनो न विमुखा मित्रार्थो न च दुर्बलः ॥

sa dhanyo jīvitaṃ tasya tasya janma sujanmanaḥ | yasyārthino na vimukhā mitrārtho na ca durbalaḥ ||

English

He is fortunate; his life is a [true] life, and his birth is a good birth, he from whom petitioners do not turn away disappointed, and whose friend's purpose does not go unfulfilled through weakness53.54

20.28

Sanskrit

मद्गृहे यद् सुवर्णादि रत्नं वाहनमासनम् । यच्चान्यत् प्रीतये तस्य तद्देयमविशङ्कया ॥

madgṛhe yad suvarṇādi ratnaṃ vāhanamāsanam | yaccānyat prītaye tasya taddeyamaviśaṅkayā ||

English

Whatever there is in my house, gold and the like, jewels, vehicles, seats, and whatever else there may be, that is to be given without hesitation for his pleasure.55

20.29

Sanskrit

धिक् तस्य जीवितं पुंसो मित्राणामुपकारिणाम् । प्रतिरूपमकुर्वन् यो जीवामीत्यवगच्छति ॥

dhik tasya jīvitaṃ puṃso mitrāṇāmupakāriṇām | pratirūpamakurvan yo jīvāmītyavagacchati ||

English

Shame on the life of that man who, without doing a fitting return to friends who have helped him, thinks, "I am alive."56

20.30

Sanskrit

उपकारं सुहृद्वर्गे यो ऽपकारञ्च शत्रुषु । नृमेघो वर्षति प्राज्ञास्तस्येच्छन्ति सदोन्नतिम् ॥

upakāraṃ suhṛdvarge yo 'pakārañca śatruṣu | nṛmegho varṣati prājñāstasyecchanti sadonnatim ||

English

The wise always wish for the advancement of that man, a cloud among men57, who rains benefit on the circle of his friends and harm on his enemies.58

Sanskrit

पुत्रावूचतुः

putrāvūcatuḥ

English

20.31The two sons said: What could anyone do for him, who has accomplished all that was to be done, in whose house all petitioners are always honoured with all their desires?59

20.31

Sanskrit

किं तस्य कृतकृत्यस्य कर्तुं शक्येत केनचित् । यस्य सर्वार्थिनो गेहे सर्वकामैः सदार्च्चिताः ॥

kiṃ tasya kṛtakṛtyasya kartuṃ śakyeta kenacit | yasya sarvārthino gehe sarvakāmaiḥ sadārccitāḥ ||

English

Its English is given with 20.31, above.

20.32

Sanskrit

यानि रत्नानि तद्गेहे पाताले तानि नः कुतः । वाहनासनयानानि भूषणान्यम्बराणि च ॥

yāni ratnāni tadgehe pātāle tāni naḥ kutaḥ | vāhanāsanayānāni bhūṣaṇānyambarāṇi ca ||

English

Whatever jewels there are in his house, how could we have them in the nether world? [Where could we find] vehicles, seats and conveyances60, ornaments and garments?61

20.33

Sanskrit

विज्ञानं तत्र यच्चास्ति तदन्यत्र न विद्यते । प्राज्ञानामप्यसौ तात सर्वसन्देहहृत्तमः ॥

vijñānaṃ tatra yaccāsti tadanyatra na vidyate | prājñānāmapyasau tāta sarvasandehahṛttamaḥ ||

English

Whatever knowledge there is in that house62 is found nowhere else. Even among the wise, father63, he is the foremost remover of every doubt.64

20.34

Sanskrit

एकं तस्यास्ति कर्तव्यमसाध्यं तच्च नौ मतम् । हिरण्यगर्भगोविन्दशर्वादीनीश्वरादृते ॥

ekaṃ tasyāsti kartavyamasādhyaṃ tacca nau matam | hiraṇyagarbhagovindaśarvādīnīśvarādṛte ||

English

There is one thing that has to be done for him, and in our opinion it cannot be accomplished, except by the lords, Hiraṇyagarbha65, Govinda66, Śarva67 and the others.68

Sanskrit

पितोवाच

pitovāca

20.35

Sanskrit

पथापि श्रोतुमिच्छामि तस्य यद् कार्यमुत्तमम् । असाध्यमथवा साध्यं किं वासाध्यं विपश्चिताम् ॥

pathāpi śrotumicchāmi tasya yad kāryamuttamam | asādhyamathavā sādhyaṃ kiṃ vāsādhyaṃ vipaścitām ||

English

Even so69, I wish to hear that supreme task of his70, whether it is unachievable or achievable; or what is there that is unachievable for the wise?71

20.36

Sanskrit

देवत्वममरेशत्वं तत्पूज्यत्वञ्च मानवाः । प्रयान्ति वाञ्छितं वान्यद् दृढं ये व्यवसायिनः ॥

devatvamamareśatvaṃ tatpūjyatvañca mānavāḥ | prayānti vāñchitaṃ vānyad dṛḍhaṃ ye vyavasāyinaḥ ||

English

Human beings who are firm in resolve attain godhood, lordship over the immortals72, the state of being worshipped by them, or whatever else they desire.73

20.37

Sanskrit

नाविज्ञातं न चागम्यं नाप्राप्यं दिवि चेह वा । उद्यतानां मनुष्याणां यतचित्तेन्द्रियात्मनाम् ॥

nāvijñātaṃ na cāgamyaṃ nāprāpyaṃ divi ceha vā | udyatānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ yatacittendriyātmanām ||

English

For men who are diligent, whose minds, senses and selves are restrained, nothing is unknown, nothing unreachable, and nothing unattainable, whether in heaven or here on earth.74

20.38

Sanskrit

योजनानां सहस्राणि व्रजन् याति पितीलिकः । अगच्छन् वैनतेयो ऽपि पादमेकं न गच्छति ॥

yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi vrajan yāti pitīlikaḥ | agacchan vainateyo 'pi pādamekaṃ na gacchati ||

English

Moving along, an ant covers thousands of yojanas75; but Vainateya76, even though he is [a great flier], does not go a single step if he does not move.77†

20.39

Sanskrit
